primaryText: Suppose it's possible the keys are in the drawer but they can't be.
context: Flat-footed conjunction of 'possible phi' with 'can't phi', embedded under suppose.
comment: Observation 5: can't phi excludes 'it's possible that phi'; the conditional-antecedent variant ('If it's possible the keys are in the drawer but they can't be, then ...') is equally incoherent. If can't were weak necessity over not-phi, the conjunction should be coherent — the Mantra's dilemma. Migrated from Phenomena/Modality/EpistemicEvidentiality.lean cantPossibleContradiction.

context: Phil has cooked the dinner, checking all the food himself, and knows it is ready.
comment: §4.2 Anti-knowledge: one of the trouble-making examples from Goodhue's defense of the epistemic account, context reproduced verbatim. The authors: the extent to which (24b) is marked is the extent to which Phil has direct enough information about what is for dinner and thus about whether all the to-dos have been accomplished. Footnote 23 calls the '#' 'a little harsh': (24') 'The chicken is done, the peas are ready, and the table is set. So: Dinner must be ready.' Migrated from Phenomena/Modality/EpistemicEvidentiality.lean philCooksDinner.

context: Phil had to step out and instructed Meryl to turn the peas off when they are done and take the chicken out when the temperature is right; she does both and has seen that the table is set, but wonders whether Phil was planning to make anything else, e.g. a salad.
comment: §4.2: minimal pair with (24). The authors: the extent to which (25b) is felicitous and true tracks the extent to which Meryl's information about what is for dinner is not direct enough. Footnote 23: if she vocalizes her uncertainty about a salad, (25') '??Dinner must be ready.' Migrated from Phenomena/Modality/EpistemicEvidentiality.lean merylCooksDinner.
